statements.t: The Company now expects full-year 2026 revenue of $8 million to $9 million, compared with its previous guidance of $18 million to $22 million.

The revised guidance reflects the Company’s decision to slow the pace of deployment of its initial AI compute capacity in response to rapidly rising compute pricing, equipment costs and financing costs, which accelerated following the midterm elections.
The Company’s previous guidance assumed that initial AI compute capacity would be deployed and generating revenue in the fourth quarter of 2026.
The Company no longer expects to recognize AI compute revenue in 2026, and fourth quarter revenue is expected to be generated primarily by its commercial aircraft engine portfolio.
The Company is maintaining its full-year 2027 revenue guidance of $125 million to $175 million.
The Company will update its guidance once its Dallas and North Carolina capacity is fully contracted and the mix of customer deposits and financing is finalized.
